clue.text: Going first taking item found in newspaper

parts.note: something going first is in front, at the head of the field
an article can also mean a thing taken or a single object, so this word stands for it here

explanation.surface: Someone first in line picks up a piece they spotted in the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An editorial, the main opinion piece a newspaper runs, is called its leader.

clue.text: Leslie inside a long time is not becoming old

indicators.note: inside tells us the short name for Leslie sits within the phrase for a long time

parts.note: ages means a very long time, as in 'I waited for ages'
Les is the usual short form of the name Leslie

explanation.surface: Leslie, after a long spell, is somehow not getting any older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless never shows signs of growing older.

clue.text: Lady coming from detached area stopped short

indicators.note: stopped short means the word for detached area is cut off before its end

parts.note: an island is an area of land cut off by water

explanation.surface: A woman emerges from a cut-off area that ended abruptly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped short' removes the last two letters, ND, from ISLAND. Isla is a Scottish girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Isla is a female first name, so it can stand for a woman.

clue.text: Gun in this place had finally been picked up

parts.note: gat is old American slang for a pistol
here means in this place

indicators.note: finally says to take only the closing letter of the word had

explanation.surface: A gun in this spot had at last been collected.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather things is to collect them, lifting them up together.

clue.text: Spots Diane inside plant

indicators.note: inside says the short name for Diane goes within the word for spots

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin
Di is a common short form of Diane

explanation.surface: Diane finds spots on herself after handling a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The radish is a plant grown for its peppery root.

clue.text: Cover new body of water in Swiss town

parts.note: to inter is to bury, covering with earth
a lake is an inland body of water

explanation.surface: A new lake is covered over in a town in Switzerland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; the pieces join as INTER, LAKE, then N.
explanation.definitionFit: Interlaken is a resort town in the Bernese Oberland of Switzerland, lying between two lakes.

clue.text: Old lace left at church — and in France!

parts.note: et is the French word for and

explanation.surface: Antique lace was left at a church, and in France too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lace' here is a shoelace or thong, not the fabric: a latchet was an old word for the strap fastening a shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Latchet is an archaic term for a thong or strap that fastened a shoe or sandal.

clue.text: Plan for the job

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of, as in pros and cons
a position is a job, a post someone holds

explanation.surface: A scheme intended for the post in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal or scheme put forward for consideration is a proposition.

clue.text: Let down having puncture during performance

indicators.note: during says the word for puncture comes inside the word for performance

parts.note: a deed is something performed, an act
a flat is a punctured tyre

explanation.surface: A tyre is let down after a puncture mid-show.
explanation.definitionFit: Let down can mean emptied of air, or disappointed; deflated fits both senses.

clue.text: Word of impatience otherwise given by coach

parts.note: tut is the sound or word made in disapproval or impatience
or means otherwise, as in 'hurry or you'll miss it'

explanation.surface: An impatient remark, or something else, comes from the trainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given by' is a link phrase joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach gives private teaching, as a private teacher does.

clue.text: Right next to something in a tight spot

definitions.meaning: literally pressed up close against an object

explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase means touching some object; idiomatically it means facing great difficulty.

clue.text: Look backwards as well as forwards

indicators.note: this phrase tells us the answer reads identically in both directions, which is all the wordplay

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Glance behind you and ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to take a quick or furtive glance.

clue.text: With aspiration conspires to remove suppression

indicators.note: remove here suggests the letters being moved around into a new order

parts.note: H is an aspirate, the breathed sound, so aspiration gives the letter H

explanation.surface: Someone plots with breath and effort to lift a ban.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' and 'to' are link words. H with CONSPIRES makes ten letters, rearranged by 'remove'.
explanation.definitionFit: Censorship is the official suppressing of books, films or news thought objectionable.

clue.text: Chart that's elementary

parts.note: elementary is read not as simple but as concerning the elements, the wind and rain, so this is a chart showing them

explanation.definitionFit: A forecast chart shows the elements, meaning wind, rain and sun, so it is elementary in a punning sense.

clue.text: Thermal instrument gamester vandalised

indicators.note: something vandalised is smashed up, so the letters of the word are broken and reassembled

explanation.surface: A gambler smashed up the heating gauge.
explanation.walkthrough: Gamester means gambler. A gas meter measures gas used for heat, hence 'thermal'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas meter records how much fuel is burned for heating, so it is a heat-related device.

clue.text: Caught us playing with cat inside plant

indicators.note: inside says the rearranged word goes within the other letters

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
taken as written

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters of cat being played around with

explanation.surface: We were caught messing about with the cat in a prickly plant.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone playing with a pet; 'playing' is really the anagram signal, and 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The cactus is a spiny desert plant.

clue.text: Consumer keeping working population down

parts.note: ants form colonies of workers, so this stands for the insect
an eater is someone or something that consumes

explanation.surface: Something that eats keeps a busy colony's numbers low.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines an animal that eats ants and so keeps their numbers down, while also giving ANT and EATER.
explanation.definitionFit: This animal feeds on ants and termites, so it limits the insect colony.

clue.text: In drink nothing has been added completely

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits
O looks like zero, so it stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing is added to a drink; it is taken whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been added' is a link phrase. In toto is Latin for 'as a whole'.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means entirely or as a whole.

clue.text: Pair on occasion deceive

parts.note: a pair is two of something
a time is an occasion, as in 'that time we met'

explanation.surface: A couple on one occasion trick each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time a partner is to be unfaithful, betraying them by seeing someone else.

clue.text: Stop for a time during school time computer studies

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
a term is a division of the school year
IT, information technology, is the school subject of computer studies

explanation.surface: A break comes midway through the school term during computing lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: To intermit is to suspend or pause something for a while.

clue.text: More substantive but of less interest to vegetarians

definitions.meaning: having more substance or solid content
containing more flesh food, which people avoiding animal products would not want

explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word meaning both full of substance and containing much flesh food.

clue.text: Who included bill and Kay giving expression of

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Who included bill and Kay giving expression of (6)' is cut short after 'of' (presumably 'expression of delight'); wordplay WH(AC+K)O is clear but the definition is incomplete, and searches did not find the full text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Who included bill and Kay giving expression of

clue.text: Where composer keeps tally?

parts.note: a composer writes on music paper for a score, read here as a tally of points kept by someone recording a game

explanation.definitionFit: A record sheet for keeping points in a game; a composer's music manuscript is also a score.

clue.text: Turned gas ring for pudding

indicators.note: turned says the word gas is to be read backwards

parts.note: a ring is round, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone turns on the gas ring to cook a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned gas ring' reads as switching on a cooker burner, but 'Turned' reverses only the word before the ring. Sago pudding is a milky British school dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago is starch from palm pith, cooked with milk as a traditional British dessert.

clue.text: Star, one appearing after 30 days

indicators.note: appearing after says the letter for one is placed behind the month

parts.note: November has thirty days, abbreviated Nov
A means one, as in 'a dozen'

explanation.surface: A star turns up a month later.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares up in brightness.

clue.text: Said I omitted some form of expression

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: I left out some turn of phrase, it was said.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom is a fixed phrase whose sense differs from its words, a characteristic manner of speaking.

clue.text: Universal church

definitions.meaning: the Roman Church or one of its members

explanation.definitionFit: The word means wide-ranging or all-embracing, and also names the Roman Church.

clue.text: Don't be scalped, remain calm

definitions.meaning: literally, avoid losing the skin and hair from your head

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means don't lose your temper; literally it would mean not losing your locks to a scalping.
